capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Riga'. The Reichskommissar Hinrich Lohse sat there. After the Soviets took Riga on 13 October 1944, the rump administration held out in the Courland Pocket.

ledger.note: 25 July 1941: German civil administration of the Reichskommissariat Ostland begins. Infobox 'Established: 17 July 1941' (the Führer decree), 'Implement civil administration: 25 July 1941 at 12:00'; Generalbezirke Lithuania (Kauen), Latvia (Riga), Belarus (Minsk), later Estonia (Reval).

ledger.note: 25 July 1941: Germany governs the Reichskommissariat. The nazi-germany dossier records occupied Lithuania, Latvia and Belarus as occupation of the Soviet republics from June 1941.
5 December 1941: Estonia is added. Infobox 'Estonia added: 5 December 1941'; the Generalbezirk Estland had its seat at Reval (Tallinn).

ledger.note: 1 April 1944: Weißruthenien is detached. 'On 1 April 1944, Generalbezirk Weißruthenien was detached from Reichskommissariat Ostland'; the page does not say who took it over (it says the eastern conquered areas stayed under military control).

region.text: Lithuania without the Memel district, which the Reich held from March 1939 (Generalbezirk Litauen, seat Kauen/Kaunas)

ledger.note: July 1944: the Red Army enters Lithuania. Operation Bagration (22 June - 19 August 1944) 'retakes all of Byelorussian SSR, most of Lithuania'; Baltic offensive page: 'By 5 July, the Šiauliai offensive commenced'.

region.text: the Vilnius region (Wilna-Land and Wilna-Stadt districts of Generalbezirk Litauen)

ledger.note: 13 July 1944: Vilnius falls. 'the majority of them were lost when the city fell on 13 July'.

region.text: Kaunas, seat of the Generalbezirk Litauen

ledger.note: About 1 August 1944: Kaunas is taken. 'By 30 July all Wehrmacht resistance on the approaches to the Neman River had retreated or been annihilated.' 'Two days later the city of Kaunas was under Soviet control' (the page gives no date); the Kaunas offensive ran 'from 28 July to 28 August'.

17-26 September 1944: mainland Estonia is cleared. The Tallinn offensive (17–26 September 1944) 'to drive German forces from mainland Estonia'; Operation Aster 'aimed at the evacuation of Army Group North from mainland Estonia'.

region.text: Latvia except the Courland Pocket, with Riga

ledger.note: 13 October 1944: Riga falls. Infobox 'Soviets reoccupied Riga: 13 October 1944'. The Riga offensive (14 September - 24 October 1944) 'cleared the eastern coast of the Gulf of Riga'.

region.text: Samogitia (Žemaitija), the west of Lithuania, outside the Memel district

ledger.note: October 1944: western Lithuania is cut off and lost. The Memel offensive (5–22 October 1944) 'was an attack by the 1st Baltic Front aimed at severing the connection between the German Army Groups Centre and North'; the pages give no dates for Šiauliai or Telšiai. Confidence 1: the month bridges a silence.

region.text: Lithuania without the Memel district, which the Reich held from March 1939 (Generalbezirk Litauen, seat Kauen/Kaunas)

ledger.note: October 1944: the fighting in Lithuania ends with the Soviet breakthrough to the Baltic coast and the Courland Pocket's formation ('Formation of the Courland Pocket: 15–22 October 1944'). Confidence 1.

region.text: the Courland Pocket, where 'the rump administration of Ostland held out'

ledger.note: 15-22 October 1944: the Courland Pocket forms. 'Communication lines between Army Group North and Army Group Centre were permanently severed'; formation of the pocket 15–22 October 1944.

region.text: the Estonian islands of Hiiumaa, Saaremaa and Muhu

ledger.note: 27 September - 24 November 1944: the Moonsund Landing takes the Estonian islands. 'the amphibious landing on the Estonian islands of Hiiumaa, Saaremaa and Muhu'; the page gives the operation's dates, not the dates of capture.

region.text: the Courland Pocket, where 'the rump administration of Ostland held out'

ledger.note: 10 May 1945: the Courland Pocket surrenders. 'German forces including the rump administration of Ostland held out in the Courland Pocket until 10 May 1945, two days after the German surrender'; the Baltic offensive page has 'the surrender of the Army Group Courland on 9 May 1945'.

region.text: the Courland Pocket, where 'the rump administration of Ostland held out'

ledger.note: 10 May 1945: German rule in the Baltic ends with the surrender of the Courland Pocket.

region.text: the Courland Pocket, where 'the rump administration of Ostland held out'

ledger.note: 10 May 1945: the last of the Reichskommissariat Ostland ends. The infobox gives 'Formally dissolved: 21 January 1945'; the rump held out in Courland until 10 May 1945.

wars.name: Operation Bagration

zones.text: Lithuania without the Memel district, which the Reich held from March 1939 (Generalbezirk Litauen, seat Kauen/Kaunas)

wars.outcome: The Red Army retakes Belarus and most of Lithuania between 22 June and 19 August 1944: Minsk on 3 July (the page also says 4 July), Vilnius on 13 July, Kaunas about 1 August, the Gulf of Riga coast on 31 July.
wars.note: Weißruthenien had been detached from Ostland on 1 April 1944, so Belarus is not a loss of this state; only Lithuania counts.

wars.name: Baltic offensive
wars.outcome: The Baltic strategic offensive (14 September - 24 November 1944) clears mainland Estonia (17-26 September), the Estonian islands (27 September - 24 November) and Riga (13 October) and seals Army Group North into the Courland Pocket (15-22 October).
wars.note: The Courland Pocket held until the surrender of 9/10 May 1945.

certainty.note: The Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian Generalbezirke follow the borders of the Soviet republics; Weißruthenien's borders are not on the page and its eastern edge was a military-governance line (soft).
The edge is the Soviet front, which the pages date by offensives, not by line.

sources.title: Reichskommissariat Ostland
sources.note: Identity, 17 July / 25 July 1941, Estonia added 5 December 1941, Weißruthenien detached 1 April 1944, Riga 13 October 1944, dissolved 21 January 1945, Courland until 10 May 1945. No area figure.

sources.title: Baltic offensive
sources.note: 14 September - 24 November 1944; Tallinn offensive 17-26 September; Riga offensive; Moonsund; Memel offensive 5-22 October; Courland Pocket 15-22 October; surrender 9 May 1945.

sources.title: Operation Bagration
sources.note: 22 June - 19 August 1944; Minsk 3/4 July, Vilnius 13 July, Kaunas about 1 August, Gulf of Riga 31 July.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the Reichskommissariat; the nazi-germany dossier draws occupied Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Belarus from Cliopatria's 1942 shapes as occupation of the Soviet republics, so the rendering step must not draw both. The page gives no area or population (page silent). Generalbezirk Weißruthenien (Minsk) is read as the Minsk and Grodno oblasts, an approximation; the page names West Belarus and Nowogródek but not borders; Bezirk Białystok and Vilnius-Memel arrangements are not on the pages. The page lists end of existence as 'Formally dissolved: 21 January 1945' and the rump held out in the Courland Pocket to 10 May 1945; the dossier ends at 10 May 1945 because the land was still held. The Baltic offensive page gives offensive dates, not the capture days of Tallinn or Riga; Riga's 13 October comes from the Ostland infobox. The Lithuanian losses are dated from Operation Bagration only to the month; the west of Lithuania is a confidence-1 bridge. Region names the gazetteer may lack: none.
